1 لَبِدَ , aor.
لَبَدَ , inf. n. لَبَدٌ, It (a thing) stuck, clave, or adhered. (Msb.) ―
-b2- لَبَدَ بِالأَرْضِ, aor,
لَبُدَ , inf. n. لُبُودٌ; (S, L;) and بِهَا ↓ البد ; (L;) and بِهَا ↓ تلبّد ; (S;) It (a thing) stuck, clave, or adhered, to the ground. (S, L.) ―
-b3- بِالأَرْضِ ↓ تلبّد He (a bird) lay upon his breast, cleaving to the ground. (S, L, K.) ―
-b4- (tropical:) He clave to the ground, concealing his person. (A.) ―
-b5- Hence the proverb تَصَيَّدِى ↓ تَلَبَّدِى , [for تَتَصَيَّدِى, (tropical:) Cleave thou (addressed to a female) to the ground: thou wilt take, or catch, or snare, or entrap, game]. (A.) ―
-b6- Hence also, ↓ تلبّد (tropical:) He remained fixed, or steady, and looked, or considered. (A.) ―
-b7- لَبَدَ بِالمَكَانِ, (L, K, *) aor.
لَبُدَ , inf. n. لُبُودٌ; and لَبِدَ, aor.
لَبَدَ , inf. n. لَبَدٌ; (L, K;) and ↓ البد ; (S, L, K;;) (tropical:) He remained, continued, stayed, abode, or dwelt, in the place; (S, L, K; *) and clave to it. (L, K. *) ―
-b8- لَبَدَ عَلَى عَصَاهُ, inf. n. لُبُودٌ, (assumed tropical:) He (a pastor) leaned upon his staff, remaining fixed to his place. (L.) ―
-b9- لَبِدَ, aor.
لَبَدَ , (S, L,) inf. n. لَبَدٌ, (S, L, K,) He (a camel) became choked by eating much of the plant called صِلِّيَان, suffering a contortion in the [part of the chest called] حَيْزُوم and in the [part of the throat called] غَلْصَمَة: (ISk, S, L, K: *) or had a complaint of the belly from eating of the قَتَاد [or tragacantha]. (AHn, L.) ―
-b10- See 4.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
